metadata.title: Tokyo Neighborhood Explorer - Find Your Perfect Area
metadata.description: Interactive map of Tokyo neighborhoods rated by food, nightlife, transport, rent, safety, parks, and more. Find the best area to live in Greater Tokyo.

ratingTooltips.food: Variety and quality of restaurants, cafes, street food, and specialty dining within 10-15 min walk
ratingTooltips.nightlife: Bars, izakaya, clubs, live music venues, and late-night entertainment options
ratingTooltips.transport: Number of train lines, frequency, connections to major hubs, and overall commute convenience
ratingTooltips.rent: Affordability based on actual rent data (1K-1LDK). 10 = cheapest (~¥70k/mo), 1 = most expensive (~¥300k+)
ratingTooltips.safety: Overall neighborhood safety: crime rates, street lighting, family-friendliness, late-night comfort
ratingTooltips.green: Parks, gardens, riverside walks, green spaces, and nature within 15 min walk
ratingTooltips.gym_sports: Fitness centers, gyms, sports facilities, running paths, and athletic amenities nearby
ratingTooltips.vibe: Overall character and charm: cultural identity, street life, local community, architectural interest
ratingTooltips.crowd: Quietness level (inverted: 10 = very peaceful and uncrowded, 1 = extremely busy and packed)
ratingTooltips.daily_essentials: Supermarkets, pharmacies, clinics, banks, laundry, dentists, and other daily necessities within walking distance

howRatingsWork.title: How ratings work
howRatingsWork.summary: Ratings are based on real data scraped from HotPepper, OpenStreetMap, MLIT, Suumo, and other sources, then normalized across 1,493 Greater Tokyo stations. The colored dots next to each rating show how deep the underlying data goes.

editorialBadge.label: Curated
editorialBadge.tooltip: This station's ratings were set by a human researcher using qualitative assessment, not purely from scraped data.

elevationTiers.very_low: Very low — check flood hazard maps

elevationTooltips.belowSea: Below sea level — this area is in a known flood-prone zone. The Koto/Edogawa lowlands and Arakawa floodplain are at highest risk during typhoons and storm surges.
elevationTooltips.veryLow: Very low elevation — near or below sea level. These areas are susceptible to flooding during heavy rainfall, typhoons, and storm surges. Check Tokyo/prefecture flood hazard maps.
elevationTooltips.low: Low-lying area. Some flood risk during extreme weather events. Generally manageable with proper preparation.
elevationTooltips.moderate: Moderate to high elevation. Lower flood risk from river/coastal flooding.

seismicTooltips.veryHigh: This area has significantly higher risk, often due to soft alluvial soil or reclaimed land that amplifies seismic waves.
seismicTooltips.high: This is a relatively high-risk area. Building earthquake resistance and emergency preparedness are important considerations.
seismicTooltips.moderate: Moderate risk. Standard earthquake preparedness measures are recommended.
seismicTooltips.low: Lower risk area, typically on firmer bedrock. Standard precautions still apply.

apiAccess.title: API Access
apiAccess.heading: Programmatic access to Tokyo data
apiAccess.intro: This site is also available as an MCP server — Anthropic's open protocol for connecting AI assistants to data and tools. Request a key below, and once approved you can use it from Claude Desktop, Claude Code, or any MCP-compatible client.
apiAccess.feature1: Ratings, confidence levels, and source provenance for all 1,493 stations
apiAccess.feature2: Full station profiles: rent, transit, environment, livecams, multilingual descriptions
apiAccess.feature3: Semantic search and find-similar in EN/JA/RU (multilingual-e5-large embeddings)
apiAccess.feature4: Hybrid recommendations combining natural-language intent with hard filters
apiAccess.step1: Submit the form. We generate an API key, hash it, and store the hash in our database.
apiAccess.step2: Your request enters a pending state. We review for abuse before activating.
apiAccess.step3: Once active, send the key as an Authorization Bearer header to city-rating.pogorelov.dev/mcp.
apiAccess.useCasePlaceholder: What are you building? Helps us approve faster.
apiAccess.successPending: Your key is in pending state. We'll notify you by email once it's active. The MCP will reject requests from pending keys.
apiAccess.yourKey: Your API key — save this NOW
apiAccess.saveWarning: This key will not be shown again. Store it in a password manager.
apiAccess.claudeDesktop: For Claude Desktop / Code, see the MCP README for the full configuration snippet.

metadata.title: Bangkok District Explorer — Find the Best Area to Live
metadata.description: All 50 Bangkok districts rated on transport, rent, daily essentials, food, nightlife, parks and more — built from OpenStreetMap and Overture Maps data, with the BTS / MRT network on the map.

district.metaDescriptionFallback: Living in {name}, Bangkok: ratings, rent, rail access and commute times.
district.scoreTooltip: Weighted score with default weights, relative to Bangkok's 50 districts
district.nearbyCount: {count, plural, =0 {nothing within 800 m} one {# station just outside} other {# stations just outside}}
district.railCaption: BTS, MRT, Airport Rail Link and SRT Red Line stations inside the district or on its boundary road.
district.noRailText: No rail station in this district — daily life runs on buses, boats, songthaews and motorbike taxis.
district.ratingsCaption: Bar fill compares this district to the median of Bangkok's 50 districts — hover the bar for detail, the category name for what it measures. Dots show how firm each score is.
district.barTooltipDev: Bangkok norm is {median} — this district is {dev} {direction} norm.
district.barTooltipDevExact: Bangkok norm is {median} — this district is exactly average.
district.rentTooltip: Affordability from typical 1-bedroom condo asking rents (researcher estimate). 10 = cheapest (≈ ฿8k/mo), 1 = most expensive (≈ ฿38k+)
district.howRatingsWork: Each district is covered by a 200 m grid. Every point records what a resident there can reach on foot — places to eat, shops, clinics, gyms, parks — plus distance to rail and a modelled peak-hour commute to five hubs. Points in built-up areas count fully, empty fields barely. Places come from two independent sources, OpenStreetMap and Overture Maps. Rent and safety are researcher estimates: Bangkok publishes no open district-level data for them.
district.relativeNote: Scores are relative within Bangkok's 50 districts: a Bangkok 8 is not comparable with a Tokyo 8.
district.factsSource: Counts inside the district boundary, approximate. Places: Overture Maps Places (CDLA-Permissive-2.0); parks and piers: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL). Population and area: Department of Provincial Administration registration via Wikidata — registered residents undercount central districts.
district.noRailNearbyText: No station inside the district itself — the nearest ones are just outside its edge (below).

station.metaDescription: Living near {name} station ({district}, Bangkok): ratings for the walkable area around the station, rent, rail lines and commute times.
station.scoreTooltip: Weighted score with default weights, relative to Bangkok's station areas
station.stationsCaption: The station this area is built around, and the lines that stop there.
station.interchangeCaption: An interchange: these stations are a short walk apart, so they share one area.
station.ratingsCaption: The area is everything within 800 m of the station that is closer to it than to any other station. Bar fill compares it with the median of Bangkok's station areas — hover the bar for detail, the category name for what it measures.
station.barTooltipDev: Bangkok norm is {median} — this area is {dev} {direction} norm.
station.barTooltipDevExact: Bangkok norm is {median} — this area is exactly average.
station.rentTooltip: Affordability from typical 1-bedroom condo asking rents — the district estimate, blended by residents where the area spans two districts. 10 = cheapest (≈ ฿8k/mo), 1 = most expensive (≈ ฿38k+)
station.howRatingsWork: The station area uses the same 200 m grid as the districts: every point records what a resident there can reach on foot — places to eat, shops, clinics, gyms, parks — plus a modelled peak-hour commute to five hubs. The area's score is the resident-weighted average of its points, ranked against Bangkok's other station areas. Places come from two independent sources, OpenStreetMap and Overture Maps. Rent and safety have no open street-level data, so they are the district estimates.
station.relativeNote: Scores are relative within Bangkok's station areas: they are not comparable with district scores, nor with Tokyo.
station.factsSource: Counts inside the station area (≤ 800 m, nearest station), approximate. Places: Overture Maps Places (CDLA-Permissive-2.0); parks and piers: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).
station.districtsCaption: The districts this station area covers, by share of its residents — rent and safety come from their estimates.
station.viewGrid: See it on the 200 m grid →
